meta.title: Microengineered perfusable 3D-bioprinted glioblastoma model for in vivo mimicry of tumor microenvironment.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A perfusable, vascularized glioblastoma model was printed with patient-derived tumour cells, astrocytes and microglia in a fibrin/gelatin bioink, and used to predict drug responses.

formulations.name: Fibrin 3D-bioink (1% fibrinogen + 6% gelatin)
formulations.key_outcome: A perfusable printed glioblastoma model with stromal cells mimicked tumour growth and drug response.

evidence.quote: Young’s modulus of 24.5 ± 2.6 kPa was achieved when the final gelatin concentration was 6% (w/v)
constant fibrinogen [1% (w/v)], Th (0.5 U/ml), and TG [3% (w/v)] and gelatin at serial concentrations
was mixed with Azurite-labeled PD-GB4 cells (1 × 106 cells/ml), GFP-labeled hAstro (1 × 106 cells/ml), and hMG (1 × 105 cells/ml)
